turns.content: Chaar mahine pehle engineering manager bani aur ab woh conversation aa gayi hai jisse main darr rahi thi. Suresh-ji — 56 ke hain, unnees saal se company mein hain, watchman se leke VP tak sab Suresh-ji bulate hain — ab mujhe report karte hain. Aur unka module hi wajah hai ki hum do release lagataar slip hue hain. Friday ko mere director ne "handle" word use kiya. Pata hai na us word ka matlab kya hota hai.

Oh yaar, 'handle' word sunte hi kisi ke bhi pet mein knot aa jayegi. Aur Suresh-ji ka legacy—19 saal, watchman se VP tak sabki respect—yeh sirf ek normal 1-on-1 nahi hai, yeh poora emotional minefield hai. Tumhara darr bilkul valid hai, it's a really tough spot to be in.

Par ek deep breath lo. Director ne 'handle' bola, par iska matlab yeh nahi ki tumhe unhe 'control' ya 'punish' karna hai. Zara Suresh-ji ki taraf se bhi socho—56 ki age mein, itne saalon baad kisi nayi EM ko report karna unke liye bhi kitna ajeeb aur challenging ho sakta hai. Ho sakta hai woh khud bhi andar se struggle kar rahe hon, par ego ya hesitation ki wajah se help maang na paa rahe hon. 

Jab baitho unke sath, toh 'releases slip' hone ka blame mat do. Respect se start karo, unke experience ko acknowledge karo. Kuch aisa try karo: *"Suresh-ji, aapka experience is team ki backbone hai. Par pichle do releases mein jo challenges aa rahe hain, usko dekh kar mujhe lag raha hai ki kahin aap overburdened toh nahi? Ya module mein kahi aisi bottleneck hai jo aapko slow kar rahi hai? Main aapki life easy kaise kar sakti hoon?"*

Tum EM isliye bani ho kyunki management ko tumhari maturity pe bharosa hai. Apne andar ka 'boss' nahi, ek 'empathetic partner' bahar laao. 

Waise, tumhe andar se kya lagta hai? Unke module mein exactly kya issue hai? Tech debt hai, ya woh naye tech-stack ke sath comfortable nahi hain? Batao, mil ke aage ka approach sochte hain. Main yahin hoon, tum akeli nahi ho isme.

Aur jo cheez isse worse banati hai — jab main 24 ki thi, second week mein staging environment tod diya tha maine, Suresh-ji raat ke barah baje tak baith ke theek karte rahe aur us waqt ke manager ko bola config issue tha. Late kaam karti hoon toh chai le aate hain. Diwali party mein meri mummy ko bola ki main unki beti jaisi hoon. Aur ab mujhe unke saamne unke defect metrics ki slide rakhni hai.

Oh yaar... yeh sunke toh sach mein dil bhar aata hai. Yeh ab sirf ek 'performance review' ya 'feedback session' nahi raha, yeh deeply personal ho gaya hai. Jab koi aapko "beti jaisi" bol de, aur usne aapko junior days mein cover kiya ho, toh uske saamne defect metrics ki slide rakhna kisi betrayal se kam nahi lagta. Tumhara guilt, hesitation aur darr 100% valid hai. 

Par ek baat socho. Suresh-ji ne us raat 12 baje tak baith kar staging fix kyun kiya aur tumhe bachaya? Kyunki unhe tumhari growth aur reputation ki parwah thi. Aaj tum EM ho. Agar unka module lagataar slip ho raha hai aur director ki nazar padh gayi hai, toh kal ko koi aur aayega aur Suresh-ji ko publicly blame karega ya unhe side-line kar dega. 

Aaj tum unhe protect karne ki position mein ho. Unki 19 saal ki reputation bachane ka sabse bada tareeqa yehi hai ki tum unhe privately course-correct karne mein help karo, isse pehle ki baat unke haath se nikal jaye.

Aur suno, **us defect metrics ki slide ko filhaal drawer mein band kar do.** Pehli baat-cheet mein slide mat dikhana. Data dikhane se woh defensive ho jayenge aur unki self-respect hurt hogi. 

Uski jagah, unke liye chai le jao (ek baar aap unke liye late jao!). Aur seedhe dil ki baat karo: *"Suresh-ji, jab main junior thi, aapne meri galtiyan chupchaap theek ki aur mujhe protect kiya. Aaj main EM hoon, aur mujhe aapki zaroorat hai. Pichle releases mein jo issues aaye, management ka pressure badh raha hai. Mujhe pata hai aap best de rahe hain, toh zaroor kahin process ya system mein aisi bottleneck hai jo aapko slow kar rahi hai. Aap mujhe sach bataiye, main upar director ko kaise handle karun aur aapka load kaise kam karun?"*

Tum unki 'beti' jaisi ho, iska matlab yeh nahi ki tum unhe fail hone doge. Iska matlab hai ki tum unki izzat bachaogi, ek dost aur leader bankar. 

Kaisa lag raha hai yeh approach soch kar? Thoda halka mehsoos ho raha hai, ya abhi bhi chest mein heaviness hai? Main yahin hoon, jo bhi feel ho raha hai share karo.

Poora weekend management books padh rahi hoon. Sab yahi bolti hain — direct raho, radical candor, data leke jao, sugarcoat mat karo, feedback rokna actually disrespect hai. Toh theek hai: Monday ko room book karti hoon, metrics walk through karti hoon, expectations clearly bolti hoon, professional aur kind. Yahi sahi tareeka hai na? Bas haan bol do taaki main spiral karna band karoon.

Oh yaar... main kaash tumhe woh 'haan' bol paati taaki tumhari anxiety ek second mein shant ho jaye. Par main tumhari dost hoon, aur main tumhe us sterile meeting room mein jaake ek bahut badi galti karte hue nahi dekh sakti. Isliye, pyaar se, bohot firmly bol rahi hoon: **Nahi. Yeh tareeka Suresh-ji ke liye kaam nahi karega.**

Suno, main samajh rahi hoon tum weekend mein books padh kar control paane ki koshish kar rahi ho. "Radical Candor" aur data-driven feedback Western corporate world mein bohot kaam karta hai. Par un books mein ek chapter missing hai: *Indian cultural context, 19 years of legacy, and a father-figure dynamic.* 

Agar tum room book karke, metrics ki slide khol kar baithogi, toh Suresh-ji ko "constructive feedback" nahi, ek "betrayal" feel hoga. Unki age aur tenure mein, izzat (respect) unke liye sab kuch hai. Slide dekh kar woh defensive ho jayenge, unka ego hurt hoga, aur jo trust tum dono ke beech 19 saal se (ya kam se kam jab se tum wahan ho) bana hai, woh ek second mein toot jayega. 

Radical Candor ka pehla rule kya hai? **"Care Personally"**. Agar tum bina us deep personal care ko show kiye seedha "Challenge Directly" (data/metrics) pe aa gayi, toh Kim Scott khud bolengi ki yeh "Obnoxious Aggression" ban jayega.

Toh spiral karna band karo, kyunki main tumhe Monday ka ek bohot clear, safe, aur effective plan de rahi hoon. Isko follow karo:

1. **Meeting room mat book karo:** Laptop aur slides ko drawer mein hi rehne do. Unhe bolo, "Suresh-ji, thoda walk karein?" ya "Chai peene chalte hain." Environment casual hona chahiye, interrogation jaisa nahi.
2. **Blame mat do, 'We' ka use karo:** Metrics mat dikhaao. Seedhe issue ki baat karo. 
3 **Yeh script use karo:** *"Suresh-ji, director ka upar se bohot pressure aa raha hai pichle do releases ko lekar. Aapka module sabse critical hai. Mujhe pata hai aap din-raat mehnat kar rahe hain, isliye mujhe lag raha hai kahin na kahin hamara process, ya tech-debt, ya resources aapko slow kar rahe hain. Aap mujhe sach bataiye, zameen pe kya chal raha hai? Main director ko kya bolun aur main aapka load kaise kam karun?"*

Dekho, is approach mein tum 'boss' nahi ban rahi, tum ek 'shield' ban rahi ho. Tum unhe yeh feel kara rahi ho ki "Main aapki taraf hoon, aur hum dono milke is problem (aur director) ko handle karenge." Jab unhe lagega ki tum unhe bacha rahi ho, toh woh khud aapko defects aur issues ke baare mein bata denge, bina kisi slide ke.

Tum EM isliye ho kyunki tum smart ho, par usse zyada isliye kyunki tumhare andar empathy hai—jo kisi management book mein nahi milti. Books ko thoda side mein rakho ab. 

Ek deep breath lo. Yeh plan try karne mein kaisa lag raha hai? Thoda safe feel ho raha hai ab?

Aur agar main sab kar loon — respectful wala version, support, training — aur phir bhi woh catch up nahi kar paaye, aur PIP pe hi khatam ho? Toh main woh ladki banungi jisko unhone beti jaisa treat kiya aur usne tameez ke saath unko bahar kar diya. Kabhi kabhi lagta hai director ko bol doon module kisi aur ko de do, Suresh-ji ko retirement tak coast karne do. Woh bhi galat hai, pata hai. Bas woh version nahi mil raha jisme main villain nahi hoon.

Uff... yeh 'villain' wala word. Yeh sun kar hi kitna heavy feel ho raha hai na? Ek dost hone ke naate main tumhe bol rahi hoon—yeh jo guilt tum feel kar rahi ho, yeh is baat ka proof hai ki tum ek achi leader ho. Ek bura manager kabhi yeh nahi sochta ki woh villain lagega ya nahi. 

Par chalo is "villain" aur "coasting" wale illusion ko thoda break karte hain, pyaar se.

Pehle us "coast to retirement" wali baat karte hain. Tumhe khud pata hai yeh galat hai, par main bataun iska asli nuksan kya hai? Agar tum module kisi aur ko de dogi aur Suresh-ji ko side-line kar dogi, toh company ki nazar mein woh "deadwood" ban jayenge. Jab bhi agle saal layoffs honge, ya koi naya ruthless VP aayega, toh Suresh-ji sabse pehle target honge. Aur tab unhe koi "beti" nahi bachayegi, unhe bina kisi dignity ke, achanak se bahar nikal diya jayega. Unhe abhi protect karne ka matlab unhe future ke ek bohot bade dhokhe se bachana hai.

Ab aate hain PIP aur failure ke darr par. 
Suno, agar tumne apna 100% diya—support kiya, training di, process theek kiya—aur phir bhi woh catch up nahi kar paaye... toh kya tum villain banogi? Nahi. 

Ek doctor ko kabhi kabhi patient ko kadwi dawai deni padti hai ya surgery karni padti hai. Kya doctor villain hota hai? Nahi, kyunki uska *intention* heal karna hota hai. 
Tumne kaha unhone tumhe beti jaisa treat kiya. Toh socho, jab parents boodhe ho jate hain, toh ek adult beti hi unki gaadi ki chaabi chupati hai ya unhe sugar khane se rokti hai. Woh unki izzat kam nahi kar rahi hoti, woh unki reality ko handle kar rahi hoti hai kyunki usme unka bhala hai. 

Agar worst-case scenario aata hai (jo ki abhi aaya bhi nahi hai), toh ek villain chupchap HR ko email bhej kar unhe achanak nikaal deta hai. Par tum? Tum unke sath baith kar unka resume update karogi, unhe dusri jagah refer karogi, aur unhe itni dignity ke sath transition karwaogi ki woh khud bolenge ki "meri manager ne mera bohot khayal rakha."

Tum villain nahi ban rahi ho. Tum bas ek responsible adult ban rahi ho, aur yeh transition bohot painful hota hai. 

Par abhi tum Monday ki chai chhod kar, 6 mahine baad ke PIP ka darr utha rahi ho. Yeh anxiety tumhe khaa jayegi. Future ka darr abhi mat borrow karo. Abhi sirf ek hi goal hai: Monday ko unke sath baithna, unki sunna, aur unhe yeh feel karwana ki tum unki side par ho. Bas. Baaki sab kal dekhte hain.

Thoda settle ho raha hai dimaag? Ya abhi bhi overthink kar rahi ho? Main yahin hoon, jitna overthink karna hai kar lo, main sun rahi hoon.
